claim: CRC is one of the most common malignancies in the Western world.

claim: The occurrence of metastasis after the operation is the leading cause of poor prognosis for CRC patients.

evidence: Supported by citation to Yoshii et al., 2014

claim: Rio kinase is a relatively conserved family of atypical serine/threonine kinases.
source: Rio (right open reading frame) kinase is a relatively conserved family of atypical serine/threonine kinases (LaRonde-LeBlanc and Wlodawer, 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to LaRonde-LeBlanc and Wlodawer, 2005

claim: RIOK1 and RIOK2 are two members of the Rio family, named for yeast (S. cerevisiae) Rio1p and Rio2p, respectively.

claim: RIOK3 has greater similarity to RIOK1, but is only known to exist within multicellular eukaryotes.

claim: Rio kinases lack substrate binding loops and an activation loop.

claim: The RNA Polymerase subunit Rpa43 in yeast has been identified as the first Rio1 substrate.

claim: RIOK1 knockout is lethal and was identified being an essential gene in yeast.

claim: RIO kinases are required for the survival of Ras-dependent cancer cells.

claim: RIOK1 was overexpressed in colon cancer cells and promoted cell proliferation in vitro in the context of human CRC.

claim: Lysine methylation acts as a novel regulatory mechanism to control protein functions.

evidence: Supported by citation to Oudhoff et al., 2013

claim: Lysine methylation is primarily catalyzed by a family of protein methyltransferases containing a catalytic SET domain.
source: Although there are about 50 lysine methyltransferases in mammals, lysine methylation is primarily catalyzed by a family of protein methyltransferases containing a catalytic SET domain (Dillon et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dillon et al., 2005

evidence: Supported by citations to Fu et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016

claim: Methylation of HIF-1α stimulates HIF-1α proteasomal degradation.

evidence: Supported by citations to Fu et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016

claim: RIOK1 can be regulated by phosphorylation.

evidence: Supported by citation to Angermayr et al., 2007

claim: RIOK1 mRNA levels increased an average 6.15-fold in metastasis lymph node samples versus normal tissues.
source: The scatter diagram demonstrated the increase of RIOK1 mRNA levels in CRC and metastasis lymph node samples versus normal tissues, with an average 4.03-fold and 6.15-fold increase respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1B

claim: The percentage of cells expressing RIOK1 were 25%, 52.2%, 67.7%, and 87.8% in cancer stage I, II, III, and IV of CRC, respectively.

claim: High levels of RIOK1 expression are significantly correlated to disease-free survival (DFS; p=0.001).

claim: An increased expression of RIOK1 was observed in gastric cancer (GC) tissues.

evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: RIOK1 may function as an oncogene in CRC development.
source: Collectively, our data show that the RIOK1 expression is frequently upregulated in CRC and GC, and correlated with poor prognosis, suggesting that RIOK1 may function as an oncogene in CRC development.

claim: The levels of endogenous RIOK1 were significantly higher in CRC cell lines than in normal intestinal epithelial cells (IECs).
source: It was observed that the levels of endogenous RIOK1 were significantly higher in CRC cell lines than in normal intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) (Figure 2A).

claim: Down-regulation of RIOK1 significantly inhibited the proliferation rate of HCT116 cells compared to negative control.

claim: Both migration and invasion were obviously inhibited in RIOK1 knock-down HCT116 cells.

claim: Overexpression of RIOK1 in RKO had opposite effects on cell viability compared to knockdown.

evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2I

claim: RIOK1 knockdown strongly upregulated the expression of E-cadherin.
source: Cells with relatively high RIOK1 expression displayed a mesenchymal-like phenotype, and the expression of vimentin (a mesenchymal marker) was enhanced, while RIOK1 knockdown strongly upregulated the expression of E-cadherin (an epithelial marker) (Figure 2I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2I

claim: RIOK1 knockdown significantly inhibited the tumorigenesis of CRC cells compared with the control in an in vivo tumor formation assay.
source: Importantly, an in vivo tumor formation assay demonstrated that RIOK1 knockdown significantly inhibited the tumorigenesis of CRC cells compared with the control (Figure 2J).
evidence: Supported by in vivo tumor formation data shown in Figure 2J

claim: RIOK1 overexpression enhanced the RKO cell growth rate.
source: Conversely, RIOK1 overexpression enhanced the RKO cell growth rate (Figure 2K).
evidence: Supported by in vivo tumor growth data shown in Figure 2K

claim: SETD7 was identified as a RIOK1-interacting protein from LC-MS/MS analysis.

claim: Co-IP assay confirmed the binding of SETD7 to RIOK1 at endogenous expression levels in RKO cells.

claim: SETD7 may directly monomethylate RIOK1.

claim: The methylation of RIOK1 was almost abolished in the HEK293T-shSETD7 cells compared with the HEK293T-shcontrol cells.

claim: SETD7 methylates RIOK1 in vivo.

claim: SETD7 methylates RIOK1 in vitro.

claim: The identified RIOK1 methylation sequence was evolutionarily conserved.

claim: K411R mutation almost completely abolished RIOK1 methylation by SETD7 in vitro.

evidence: Supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 3E

claim: K411 is most likely the major, if not the sole, site within RIOK1 that is methylated by SETD7.
source: Together, our data suggest that K411 is most likely the major, if not the sole, site within RIOK1 that is methylated by SETD7.

claim: The enzymatic deficient SETD7-H297A mutant reduced the level of RIOK1-K411me1.

claim: V5-SETD7 catalyzed K411me1 for Flag-RIOK1-WT and Flag-RIOK1-K401R mutant, but not K411R mutant.

claim: The mRNA levels of RIOK1 were not changed by SETD7 overexpression.

claim: The methylation of RIOK1 may disrupt its stability.

claim: In HEK293T-sh-SETD7-1 cells, the half-life of endogenous RIOK1 was dramatically prolonged.

claim: Endogenous LSD1 was present in the RIOK1 immunocomplex in 293T and HCT116 cells.

claim: GST-RIOK1 pulled down His-LSD1 in a GST pull-down assay.

claim: LSD1 directly binds RIOK1.

claim: RIOK1 protein levels in Kdm1a−/− MEFs were greatly decreased compared with Kdm1a+/− MEFs.
